I get **Dq ≈ 1917 cm⁻¹, B ≈ 820 cm⁻¹, C ≈ 3680 cm⁻¹**, with the caveat that the three spin-allowed bands are not fitted exactly.

**Assignments (high-spin d³, ⁴A₂g ground state):**
- ⁴T₂g at 19 170 cm⁻¹ gives 10Dq directly, so Dq = 1917 cm⁻¹.
- ⁴T₁g(F) at 27 260 cm⁻¹ and ⁴T₁g(P) at 42 610 cm⁻¹ fix B. Their least-squares fit with the quartet block gives B ≈ 820 cm⁻¹.
- The spin-forbidden 17 050 cm⁻¹ band is the lowest doublet, ²Eg(a), which depends on C. Varying C at fixed Dq and B shows ²Eg(a) moves about 3 cm⁻¹ per unit of C, so C ≈ 3680 cm⁻¹ places it at 17 050 cm⁻¹.

**Fit quality:** At these values the model predicts ⁴T₁g(a) ≈ 27 227 cm⁻¹ and ⁴T₁g(b) ≈ 42 583 cm⁻¹, residuals of about 30 cm⁻¹. The built-in `ts_fit_spectrum` routine returned a different, poorer fit (Dq ≈ 1967, B ≈ 693, C left at its default of 4133, RMS ≈ 444 cm⁻¹), so I did not use its output. The three spin-allowed bands alone cannot be matched exactly with a single consistent (Dq, B) pair in this model, so B carries an uncertainty of roughly ±30–50 cm⁻¹ and C a correspondingly larger one.
